query: What visit-note signals suggest high urgency?

per_column.name: chief_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the free-text reason into clinically meaningful complaint types that differ sharply in urgency (e.g., chest_pain_cardiac, respiratory_distress vs routine_preventive). Strong grouping axis for the query. Sample values are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: symptom_onset_acuity
per_column.rationale: Onset speed (sudden_acute vs weeks_to_chronic) is a canonical urgency signal, directly relevant. Samples are mostly warranted (cough x3 days -> days, twisting injury yesterday -> hours_to_day). The MI-follow-up mapped to weeks_to_chronic is a reasonable inference; nulls for silent rows are acceptable behavior.

per_column.name: pain_severity_indicator
per_column.rationale: Pain severity is a plausible urgency correlate and offers an ordinal axis. Values track the text (acne moderate, denies chest pain -> none). The URI 'mild' assignment (low-grade fever, no explicit pain) is a mild stretch but defensible; large 'none_or_not_mentioned' bucket lowers leverage slightly.

per_column.name: hemodynamic_instability
per_column.rationale: A near-boolean flag but a highly specific, high-signal marker of true emergencies; despite near-constant distribution the rare true cases are exactly what the urgency query targets. Sample rows with stable vitals correctly marked false.

per_column.name: organ_system_involved
per_column.rationale: Provides a useful grouping dimension, though it partially overlaps with chief_complaint_category. Sample mappings are sound (knee -> musculoskeletal, cough -> respiratory). Endocrine_metabolic for an annual exam with HbA1c/lipids is a defensible inference. 'not_specified' for silent rows is correct.

per_column.name: visit_type_context
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes acute/emergency activation from routine follow-up, which is relevant to urgency. Some overlap with chief_complaint_category's chronic_disease_followup value, but emergency_activation adds distinct leverage. Sample values well grounded.

per_column.name: diagnostic_urgency_proxy
per_column.rationale: Workup intensity (stat imaging, emergent labs, ECG monitoring vs no_workup) is a strong actionable urgency signal derivable from documented orders. Samples align (MRI ordered -> stat_imaging, labs -> routine_labs_imaging). Some ordinal inference but well warranted by text.

judge.rationale: The added columns collectively give multiple genuine, urgency-relevant axes (complaint type, onset acuity, pain, hemodynamic instability, workup intensity) to group and compare on, directly serving the query. There is some redundancy between chief_complaint_category, organ_system_involved, and visit_type_context, but each still contributes a distinct grouping. Values are consistently sound readings of the source text with reasonable inferences and appropriate null/not_specified handling; no hallucinations observed in the samples.
